question:
(a) A nucleus has mass defect $0.075\,\text{u}$ and mass number $15$. Calculate its binding energy and binding energy per nucleon.
(b) Take $1\,\text{u} = 931\,\text{MeV}/c^{2}$.
(c) State what binding energy per nucleon indicates.

options.A:
(a) $E_b=\Delta m\times931=0.075\times931=69.825\,\mathrm{MeV}$. Binding energy per nucleon $=69.825/15=4.655\,\mathrm{MeV}$.
(b) $1\,\mathrm{u}=931\,\mathrm{MeV}/c^2$.
(c) Binding energy per nucleon gives the average binding of each nucleon; a larger value generally indicates a more stable nucleus.
options.C:
(a) $E_b=0.075\times931=69.825\,\mathrm{MeV}$; $E_b/A=69.825\times15=1047.375\,\mathrm{MeV}$.
(b) $1\,\mathrm{u}=931\,\mathrm{MeV}/c^2$.
(c) It indicates number of protons only.
